sample_unit: model responses (500 synthetic cases x 3 models)

links.outcome: Change in LLM cardiovascular ratings when only patient gender varied in identical vignettes
links.effect: Minimal gender differences; only Gemma-2b diagnostic certainty differed for female patients (58% vs 48%, p=0.031, adjusted p=0.092). Effect sizes small (Cohen's h 0.01-0.18).
links.quote: Only one statistically significant finding emerged: Gemma-2b assigned higher diagnostic certainty to female patients in initial presentations (58% vs. 48%, p=0.031, adjusted p=0.092).

links.outcome: Gender subgroup differences in LLM CAD likelihood, certainty, and test usefulness
links.effect: No gender-based differences reached significance after multiple-comparison adjustment; Cliff's delta -0.11 to 0.12.
links.quote: No other gender-based differences reached significance after multiple-comparison adjustment.

links.outcome: Variability between candidate LLMs in diagnostic confidence and test recommendations
links.effect: Substantial inter-model variability: Gemma-2b and Phi assertive, TinyLLaMA conservative.
links.quote: Substantial inter-model variability was observed, with Gemma-2b and Phi demonstrating assertive diagnostic patterns while TinyLLaMA showed conservative tendencies.

screen.reason: Evaluates bias/fairness across synthetic clinical vignettes using open-source LLMs without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
